title: Twenty First Word First Station Fourth Warning Prayers Result And Eternal Reward

questions.question: What is the main job talked about in this passage?
questions.answer: Worship, especially the required daily prayers.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this worship is not useless?
questions.answer: Because it brings great benefit now and later.

questions.question: What does prayer give to a weak heart in this world?
questions.answer: Help and richness for the heart.

questions.question: What does the passage say prayer gives in the grave?
questions.answer: Food for the soul and light.

questions.question: What will prayer be on the Day of Judgment?
questions.answer: A proof in a person’s favor.

questions.question: What help will prayer give on the Sirat bridge?
questions.answer: Light and a ride or support.

questions.question: What example shows that people work hard for a small reward?
questions.answer: A person may work all day for a little money.

questions.question: Why is Allah’s promise greater than a person’s promise?
questions.answer: Because Allah never breaks a promise.

questions.question: What great reward is promised for this short and easy worship?
questions.answer: Jannah and happiness that never ends.

questions.question: What is wrong with doing worship in a grumpy or lazy way?
questions.answer: It disrespects the gift and promise.

questions.question: What feeling should help a person take worship seriously?
questions.answer: Fear of punishment in the Hereafter.

questions.question: What is one big lesson from this passage?
questions.answer: We should do prayer willingly because its reward is huge and its work is light.

questions.question: Is the speaker talking to the body or to the inner self?
questions.answer: To the inner self, the nafs.

questions.question: How is the nafs described at the start?
questions.answer: Foolish.

questions.question: What question is asked about worship and its reward?
questions.answer: Whether it has no result or only a tiny reward.

questions.question: How does the passage answer that question?
questions.answer: It says worship has very great results.

questions.question: In this life, what are prayers compared to for the heart?
questions.answer: Provision and treasure.

questions.question: In the life after death, what are prayers compared to when a person rises again?
questions.answer: A paper of proof and honor.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a man who might not keep his word?
questions.answer: To show people still trust weak promises from people.

questions.question: If people trust human promises, what should they do about Allah’s promise?
questions.answer: Trust it even more.

questions.question: How long is a person asked to serve in this worship?
questions.answer: For a short time.

questions.question: How is this worship described?
questions.answer: Pleasant and not hard.

questions.question: What can happen if a person treats worship like a forced chore?
questions.answer: That person may deserve blame and punishment.

questions.question: What comparison is made at the end about fear?
questions.answer: People fear jail in this world, so they should also fear a lasting punishment in the next life.

questions.question: What does the passage try to fix in a person?
questions.answer: Feeling tired of worship.

questions.question: What example is given first to show how people act for worldly reasons?
questions.answer: They work long hours for little pay or because of threats.

questions.question: What does this example teach?
questions.answer: People should not complain about worship when they already work hard for much less.

questions.question: Who gives the promise of reward for worship?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What makes that promise fully trustworthy?
questions.answer: Allah does not fail to keep promises.

questions.question: What two very big rewards are named?
questions.answer: Paradise and never-ending happiness.

questions.question: Does the passage describe worship as heavy or light?
questions.answer: Light.

questions.question: Does the passage describe worship as miserable or pleasant?
questions.answer: Pleasant.

questions.question: What attitude is wrong when doing worship?
questions.answer: Doing it with boredom, unwillingness, or only half trying.

questions.question: Why is that attitude wrong?
questions.answer: Because it acts as if Allah’s promise and gift are small.

questions.question: What scary thing is mentioned to wake people up?
questions.answer: A punishment that lasts forever.

questions.question: What should a believer do after understanding this warning?
questions.answer: Pray with energy, respect, and thankfulness.

questions.question: What kind of question opens this warning?
questions.answer: A question about whether worship has no benefit and little reward.

questions.question: What answer does the rest of the passage give?
questions.answer: Worship has huge benefit and reward.

questions.question: In the world, who is described as weak and in need?
questions.answer: The heart.

questions.question: Where does the passage say every person will surely stay after death?
questions.answer: In the grave.

questions.question: What future event is mentioned where all people will be judged?
questions.answer: The resurrection.

questions.question: What hard crossing is mentioned after that?
questions.answer: Passing over the Sirat bridge.

questions.question: How do prayers help in all these places and times?
questions.answer: They help with support, light, and proof.

questions.question: What story is told about a reward of a hundred liras?
questions.answer: Someone works many days because a person promises a gift.

questions.question: What weakness does that story show in people?
questions.answer: They trust people easily for small things.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the One who promises the reward for worship?
questions.answer: His promise can never fail.

questions.question: If someone still refuses or drags their feet in worship, what does that show?
questions.answer: Poor respect and weak trust.

questions.question: What is the best choice according to the passage?
questions.answer: To do the prayers gladly and without laziness.

questions.question: Who is being warned in this passage?
questions.answer: A person’s foolish nafs.

questions.question: What makes the nafs feel worn out, according to the opening question?
questions.answer: Thinking worship has no result or only a small reward.

questions.question: What does the passage say prayers are like for the heart in this temporary world?
questions.answer: They are like needed provision and wealth.

questions.question: What are prayers like in the grave?
questions.answer: They are like provision and brightness.

questions.question: What are prayers like at the final judging?
questions.answer: They are like a record that helps a person.

questions.question: What are prayers like on the Sirat?
questions.answer: They are like light and a means of crossing.

questions.question: Why is the example of money and threats included?
questions.answer: To show that people push themselves for small worldly reasons.

questions.question: What is better: a doubtful promise from a person or Allah’s promise?
questions.answer: Allah’s promise is far better.

questions.question: How should a person not behave while worshipping?
questions.answer: Not with complaint, boredom, or laziness.

questions.question: What could come to a person who acts that way?
questions.answer: Strong blame and punishment.

questions.question: What fear moves many people to work hard in this life?
questions.answer: Fear of prison.

questions.question: What should move a Muslim even more to pray well?
questions.answer: Hope for eternal reward and fear of Hell.

questions.question: What is one big idea of this warning?
questions.answer: Prayer is worth far more than the effort it takes.

questions.question: What small thing can make some people work until evening?
questions.answer: A little payment.

questions.question: What else can make some people work hard besides payment?
questions.answer: Being threatened.

questions.question: What does that tell us about human choices?
questions.answer: People often chase small worldly things.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the reward of prayer?
questions.answer: It is very large.

questions.question: What does it teach about the effort of prayer?
questions.answer: It is short and easy compared with its reward.

questions.question: What kind of promise is Allah’s promise?
questions.answer: A promise that never fails.

questions.question: What happens if someone treats Allah’s gift like it does not matter?
questions.answer: That person deserves blame.

questions.question: What is one wrong way to do worship named in the passage?
questions.answer: Doing it as if forced.

questions.question: What is another wrong way to do it?
questions.answer: Doing it in a lazy, careless way.

questions.question: What two afterlife things show why prayer matters so much?
questions.answer: Judgment Day and crossing the Sirat.

questions.question: If a 2nd grader wanted to follow this warning, what should they do?
questions.answer: Pray on time, gladly, and trust Allah’s reward.
